```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4.2, dpi = if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"))) 110 else 60
)
logger::log_threshold(logger::WARN, namespace = "pdmS7")
```

A calibration describes the years it was fitted to. The model will be used in other years:
wetter, drier, after the gauge has been changed or the land drained. Two tests show whether a
calibration will hold: calibrate on one kind of year and score another, and calibrate period by
period and watch the parameters.

# The catchment

The synthetic catchment of [Counting every error fairly](fair-errors.html), over four years.

```{r data}
rain <- synthetic_rain("2016-10-01", years = 4, dt = 1, seed = 5)
truth <- modifyList(pdm_presets("standard"), list(area_km2 = 25))
model <- pdm_from_config(truth)
forcing <- rain[c("time", "rain", "pet")]
set.seed(8)
flow <- run_pdm(model, forcing[c("rain", "pet")], initial_state(model, 0.5))$output$q_m3s
observed <- flow * exp(rnorm(length(flow), 0, 0.15))
start <- modifyList(truth, list(fc = 0.8))
lower <- c(fc = 0.6, distribution.cmax = 100, surface.k1 = 1)
upper <- c(fc = 1.4, distribution.cmax = 500, surface.k1 = 30)
```

# Dry years against wet years

The differential split-sample test (Klemeš, 1986) sorts the complete water years by rain,
calibrates on the drier half and scores the wetter half, then the reverse. A model fit for the
floods of a wetter future should keep its score when it moves from dry years to wet; a large
drop means the calibration leans on conditions it will not always meet.

```{r dsst}
sst <- split_sample_test(start, forcing, observed, lower, upper, objective = "boxcox",
                         start = "soil", control = list(maxit = 40))
sst$years
sst$scores[, c("calibrated_on", "scored_on", "nse", "boxcox_nse", "volume_error")]
sst$parameters
```

Each calibration is scored twice, on its own years and on the others. Read the drop from its own
years to the others, in both directions. Here the model is right by construction, so the scores
barely move. On a real record a common failure is the volume: a calibration on dry years may
let the soil store swallow too much rain, and the volume error then grows in the wet years.

`split = "halves"` uses the first and second halves of the record instead: the classic split
sample, which tests change over time rather than climate.

# Parameters period by period

`parameter_drift()` cuts the record into runs of consecutive water years and calibrates each on
its own. Parameters the data determine stay put; a steady drift points to a change in the
catchment or the record that one long calibration would average away.

To show it working, a record in which something changes halfway: the rainfall factor `fc` goes
from 1.0 to 1.2 in October 2018, as it might if a rain gauge were replaced by one that catches
more.

```{r drift}
changed <- pdm_from_config(modifyList(truth, list(fc = 1.2)))
s0 <- initial_state(model, 0.5)
early <- run_pdm(model, forcing[c("rain", "pet")], s0)$output$q_m3s
late <- run_pdm(changed, forcing[c("rain", "pet")], s0)$output$q_m3s
cut_at <- which(forcing$time >= as.POSIXct("2018-10-01", tz = "UTC"))[1]
shifted <- c(early[seq_len(cut_at - 1)], late[seq.int(cut_at, length(late))]) *
  exp(rnorm(length(late), 0, 0.15))
drift <- parameter_drift(start, forcing, shifted, lower, upper, periods = 2,
                         objective = "boxcox", start = "soil", control = list(maxit = 40))
drift
plot(drift)
```

`fc` moves from 1.01 to 1.21, a quarter of its search range, between the two periods, and the
others stay put: the test
finds the change and says which parameter absorbed it. On a real record this is how a change of
rain gauge, of rating or of land use shows up: a tipping-bucket gauge replaced by a weighing gauge
that catches more rain, for example, appears as a step in `fc`. With three or more periods a steady slope separates a real trend from noise.

# What to do with the answer

- **A drop from dry to wet**: calibrate on a record that includes wet years, weight the floods
  with an event or threshold objective, or choose the model on forecasts in wet years
  ([Choosing a model as a forecaster](forecast-choice.html)).
- **Drift in one parameter**: find what changed. If the change is in the record, such as a new
  gauge, calibrate on the years since. If it is in the catchment, the recent years describe the
  catchment that will be forecast.
- **Drift in every parameter**: the parameters are poorly determined ([Which parameters can the
  record determine?](global-sensitivity.html)); fix the weak ones and test again.

# Cautions

- **Each half must hold floods.** A test whose wet half has no large flood says little about
  floods.
- **The tests cost a calibration each**, two for the split sample and one a period for the
  drift. The faster stages of `pdm_stages()` (`method = "dds"`, `coarse_dt`) help on long
  15-minute records.
